answer: A personal quality I believe is essential for success is perseverance, the ability to keep going despite setbacks. In my view, talent alone is rarely enough; it is [[persistence]] that ultimately makes the difference. I think this is important because the path to any worthwhile goal is inevitably filled with obstacles and failures. Anyone who expects a smooth journey is likely to give up the first time things go wrong. A close friend of mine embodies this quality perfectly; he failed several times before finally building a successful business, but he never gave up. His first venture, a small clothing shop, closed within a year, and his second barely covered its costs. What I admire is his refusal to be [[discouraged]] by temporary defeats. Each time, he studied what had gone wrong and tried again, and today he runs a thriving online shop. I have seen the same quality in my father, who kept his small business going for over thirty years through floods, price rises and difficult seasons. I genuinely believe that this kind of [[resilience]] is what separates those who succeed from those who quit. Honestly, in a world that often celebrates instant success, we forget how much quiet, stubborn effort lies behind most achievements. Perseverance keeps you moving forward when motivation fades, and motivation always fades at some point, however excited you were at the start. I think it is one of the most [[underrated]] qualities a person can have, and it is something I consciously try to [[cultivate]] in myself.

followUps.q: Do you think perseverance can be learned?
followUps.answer: I think so, mostly through experience. Every time you push through a difficulty and see the result, you become a bit more confident that you can do it again next time.

followUps.q: Is there a time you showed perseverance yourself?
followUps.answer: Getting my first job was one. I had several rejections after graduating, which was disheartening, but I kept improving my CV and interview skills until the consultancy finally offered me a position.

note: Added detail of the friend's failed ventures and comeback, and his father's thirty years in business; marked sir's existing 'cultivate'.
